practical_guide.title: Register your address

short_summary.text: Choose the correct registration procedure when moving to Leiden.

who_this_is_for.text: New arrivals staying over four months; residents changing address within the Netherlands.

when_you_need_it.text: New arrivals staying over four months; residents changing address within the Netherlands.

numbered_steps.title: Step 1
numbered_steps.body: Arriving from abroad: use Leiden’s immigration form and appointment link. Attend in person with accompanying family members. Arrange the appointment within five working days of moving.

numbered_steps.title: Step 2
numbered_steps.body: Prepare identification and proof of housing. First-time arrivals may also need civil-status certificates and legalisation; arrivals from the Dutch Caribbean need proof of deregistration.

numbered_steps.title: Step 3
numbered_steps.body: Moving within the Netherlands: notify the new municipality up to four weeks before, or within five days after, the move. Use the domestic-change procedure, not first registration.

required_documents.text: Valid ID; named purchase/rental contract or resident consent and ID copy; applicable civil-status documents.

warnings.text: Leiden lists lawful residence conditions. A short stay follows RNI rules; registration is not a residence permit.

practical_guide.disclaimer: General practical information; the responsible authority or care provider decides your individual case.

sections.title: Costs
sections.body: First registration or re-registration from abroad is free.

sections.title: Timing
sections.body: Processing an arrival from abroad takes at least five working days, depending on the case.

practical_guide.title: Get or find your BSN

short_summary.text: A BSN is issued through registration; choose resident registration or the RNI route.

who_this_is_for.text: New residents, short-stay workers or students, and people who may already have a BSN.

when_you_need_it.text: New residents, short-stay workers or students, and people who may already have a BSN.

numbered_steps.title: Step 1
numbered_steps.body: If staying over four months, register as a resident with the municipality where you live.

numbered_steps.title: Step 2
numbered_steps.body: For a stay of four months or less, check RNI eligibility. Leiden accepts European passports; people without a European passport are directed to Breda or Venlo.

numbered_steps.title: Step 3
numbered_steps.body: Complete the RNI pre-registration, keep the QR code and book an available appointment. Bring ID. If you already have a BSN, do not apply as a new RNI registration; ask the municipality which update is needed.

required_documents.text: RNI: passport or identity card, not a driving licence, plus QR code. Under-16s attend with a parent and the required legalised birth document.

numbered_steps.title: Step 1
numbered_steps.body: Check your registered address, then apply on DigiD’s official website with your BSN, birth date and address.

numbered_steps.title: Step 2
numbered_steps.body: Choose your login details and follow the phone verification steps. Keep credentials private.

practical_guide.title: Sort and dispose of household waste

short_summary.text: Use your address-specific schedule and Leiden’s own sorting rules.

who_this_is_for.text: Residents who need to find collection days or the right container.

when_you_need_it.text: Residents who need to find collection days or the right container.

numbered_steps.title: Step 1
numbered_steps.body: Enter your postcode and house number in the municipal collection schedule; check the holiday replacement dates. City-centre and suburban collection arrangements differ.

numbered_steps.title: Step 2
numbered_steps.body: In Leiden, plastic packaging, tins and drink cartons go with residual waste for later sorting. Keep glass, paper and textiles separate; check the municipal GFT instructions for your address.

numbered_steps.title: Step 3
numbered_steps.body: Do not leave bags beside a container. For bulky waste, use the Milieustraat or arrange an official collection appointment.

practical_guide.title: Emergency and non-emergency contacts

short_summary.text: Choose the contact according to the urgency and type of help.

who_this_is_for.text: Anyone in Leiden needing police, medical or municipal assistance.

when_you_need_it.text: Anyone in Leiden needing police, medical or municipal assistance.

numbered_steps.title: Step 1
numbered_steps.body: For immediate danger or a life-threatening emergency, call 112. State your location and follow the operator’s instructions.

numbered_steps.title: Step 2
numbered_steps.body: For police assistance without an emergency in the Netherlands, call 0900-8844. For urgent GP care outside normal hours, use De Limes’ postcode selector and call before travelling.

numbered_steps.title: Step 3
numbered_steps.body: For municipal questions call 14 071, or +31 71 516 5165 if the short number does not work. Use the municipal website for public-space reports.

warnings.text: Non-emergency numbers are not substitutes for 112 when immediate help is required.

practical_guide.disclaimer: General practical information; the responsible authority or care provider decides your individual case.

numbered_steps.title: Step 1
numbered_steps.body: Find the service on gemeente.leiden.nl. Its product page lists the current conditions, documents, cost and appointment option.

numbered_steps.title: Step 2
numbered_steps.body: Book through that page where required. Check the confirmation for the location; the Stadskantoor is at Bargelaan 190, not the historic Stadhuis.

numbered_steps.title: Step 3
numbered_steps.body: Use the confirmation link to change an appointment. If you need help, call the municipality; report street problems through the public-space reporting option.
